product_facts: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous data from your systems together into customer profiles, builds audiences from them and activates those audiences across channels.
Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous customer data together into profiles and builds the audiences.
A customer becomes known when they sign in: the site sends a person-level identifier, such as a CRM ID or a hashed email, with the visit, and Experience Platform stitches it into their profile.
Real-Time CDP's Adobe Target destination makes those audiences available to Target for same-page and next-page personalization, with governance and privacy support, using a datastream.

Consent and data-use rules travel with the data: the Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, and Experience Platform enforces the data usage policies you enable when audiences are activated. We would keep sensitive attributes out of those audiences unless you approve them, and never use personalization to decide eligibility or pricing.

services.name: Monthly SEO fixes with Sites Optimizer
services.scope: Each month, review new SEO opportunities in Sites Optimizer, approve or edit the suggested fixes with the content owner, deploy the content fixes to authoring for people to publish, prepare the code patches (such as Core Web Vitals fixes) and hand them to the named developer to review, test, merge and release, and report search traffic and Core Web Vitals movement in the Brand Visibility review.

source.title: Experience League: Sites Optimizer opportunity types

services.template_deliverable: Monthly fix log with each fix's route and status, and the month's search results.
services.template_acceptance: The month's agreed content fixes are in authoring, ready for the Client to publish (with Prime, applied by hand), the month's code patches are with the named developer and their status is in the fix log, and the results are reported.
services.template_assumptions:
Sites Optimizer is licensed and set up. Hours scale with the number of opportunities and sites. Sites Optimizer finds the opportunities and suggests fixes on its own.

How an approved fix is deployed depends on its opportunity: with the Ultimate package, content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) and people publish them, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches that the named developer reviews, tests, merges and releases through the existing development workflow.

Code patches arrive as pull requests or downloaded patches, by the route agreed at setup, and either way go through the Client's own review and release process; on AEM as a Cloud Service sites, broken-backlink redirects deploy through Dispatcher.

With Prime (identify and suggest only), the partner applies approved content and configuration fixes by hand, and code fixes go to the named developer with Sites Optimizer's recommendation.

These hours cover reviewing and editing the suggestions with the content owner, deploying the content fixes, preparing the code patches and handing them to the developer, and the report; the developer's review, testing, merge and release are outside these hours unless agreed.

These are the month's site fixes in one allowance, and the site fixes Brand Visibility flags (robots.txt rules for AI crawlers, redirects for pages AI agents can't reach) are made by hand in the site's configuration or redirect sheet, within the same allowance.
services.template_exclusions: The license, new content creation (a separate service), the developer's review, testing, merge and release of code patches unless agreed, and development outside AEM.
services.template_basis: One site: each month, review Sites Optimizer's new SEO opportunities, approve the fixes, deploy the content fixes, hand code patches to the developer, and report the results.
product_facts: Sites Optimizer is Adobe's cloud-based service that analyzes and improves the performance of websites built on AEM. Each opportunity it finds shows the potential business value and gives actionable recommendations.
Sites Optimizer analyzes the site and recommends improvements to its performance.

For search traffic, Sites Optimizer identifies external links that point to non-existent pages on your site and missing or faulty metadata on your pages. Its Google Search Console connector adds search rankings, click-through rates and Core Web Vitals to the analysis.

Sites Optimizer continuously monitors site performance, using Operational Telemetry to detect regressions in Core Web Vitals. Its code updates follow standard development practices, with review and approval before anything is merged into production.
Sites Optimizer applies the optimizations you select into the authoring environment only. Your AEM authors then review and publish the changes from the CMS.
Its site summary gives a snapshot of your site's performance, how Sites Optimizer has improved the site over time and the opportunities for improvement that remain.

product_facts: Experimentation Accelerator integrates with Adobe Target and Adobe Journey Optimizer to give you a centralized platform for managing, analyzing and optimizing your experiments.
Experimentation Accelerator tracks the tests from Adobe Target and Journey Optimizer in one place and recommends what to test next.

Its Experiments tab centralizes the tracking and analysis of tests from Adobe Journey Optimizer and Adobe Target, with their KPIs. For each experiment it identifies the treatment currently delivering the best performance and measures its percentage improvement over the control or baseline.

Each experiment carries a hypothesis: the planned changes to be tested and their expected impact on the primary metric. The Opportunities panel then displays AI-generated recommendations designed to enhance test performance and align with your broader business objectives.

Experimentation Accelerator only makes recommendations: it has no access to modify test settings, and every recommendation can be reviewed and edited before it is pushed out. A dedicated model is trained for every sandbox, using only your own data.

Adobe Analytics collects the data from your website and apps and reports on it.

source.title: Experience League: Integrating with Adobe Analytics

connection_how: Your AEM site is connected to an Adobe Analytics report suite, and a tags property with the Adobe Analytics extension sends page views and interactions from your pages to Analytics.
product_facts: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.
AEM Sites is where the site is built, on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, and where your authors edit its pages.
We would implement AEM Sites as a Cloud Service. Code is deployed through Cloud Manager, Adobe's one route for it, so every release passes the same code quality checks.
We would start with discovery: a review of your current site's content, templates and integrations, a named team with agreed roles, and the measures of success.

How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, we would export the content, map it to the new templates and load it into AEM, agreeing the mapping and tooling with you in discovery.

For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, check the migrated content with you, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover, with redirects for retired URLs and rollback criteria agreed beforehand.

product_facts: Journey Optimizer is Adobe's application for creating and delivering connected, personalized customer experiences across your channels. It is built on Adobe Experience Platform and its real-time customer profile, and runs both real-time journeys and scheduled campaigns.
Journey Optimizer orchestrates the journeys and campaigns and delivers the messages across channels.

We would set Journey Optimizer up in the order Adobe documents: the environment first, with a development sandbox for building and testing and a production sandbox for sending, each with its own channel configurations. Journeys are tested with test profiles before activation.

A journey automates a real-time, multi-step sequence of interactions; a campaign sends a scheduled or API-triggered message to an audience. Messages are delivered through channels like email, mobile messages, push notifications and direct mail.
Journey Optimizer tracks customer engagement and campaign performance with reports, and its reporting is integrated with Customer Journey Analytics for a clearer view of performance metrics.

When messages are sent from journeys or campaigns, your customers must always be able to unsubscribe; once they do, their profiles are automatically removed from the audience of future marketing messages. Access labels control which users can reach specific journeys, campaigns and channel configurations.

source.title: Experience League: Integrate with Adobe Analytics

connection_how: Marketo Web Personalization adds each visitor's organization, industry, segment and web campaign to your Adobe Analytics report suite, so that data shows in your Analytics reports.
product_facts: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. We would place the embed in a reusable page component, agree the fields, consent wording and validation with you, and collect only the data you approve. Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.

The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill and a PDF record of each submission, and can connect to Adobe Sign for e-signatures. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics source connector for report suite data

connection_how: A connector streams a copy of your Adobe Analytics report suite data into Adobe Experience Platform, where it builds customer profiles and audiences in Real-Time CDP. Your Analytics implementation and reports stay as they are.
product_facts: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous data from your systems together into customer profiles, builds audiences from them and activates those audiences across channels.
Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous customer data together into profiles and builds the audiences.
A customer becomes known when they sign in: the site sends a person-level identifier, such as a CRM ID or a hashed email, with the visit, and Experience Platform stitches it into their profile.
Real-Time CDP's Adobe Target destination makes those audiences available to Target for same-page and next-page personalization, with governance and privacy support, using a datastream.

Consent and data-use rules travel with the data: the Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, and Experience Platform enforces the data usage policies you enable when audiences are activated. We would keep sensitive attributes out of those audiences unless you approve them, and never use personalization to decide eligibility or pricing.
